subject: Abraham Akintola
project_type: Internal enterprise platform — governed multi-channel outbound communications
project_description: Internal platform for a UK insurance broker that centralises governed outbound customer communication across Email, SMS and WhatsApp. Built because communications were scattered with no central visibility: no one could see which customers had been contacted or whether messages arrived, failures notified nobody, and staff re-triggered sends by hand. Replaced TWO legacy systems - a Google Apps Script orchestration estate and iros-mail, a .NET 8 Azure Functions mail microservice. Provides campaign definition, approval workflow, audience sourcing, queue-backed execution, multi-provider delivery, delivery reconciliation, suppression, per-customer communication history, operational reporting, full audit trail, and a backwards-compatible API so other internal systems send through the platform rather than around it.

production_launch_date.note: First campaign send is 2026-06-26, but whether cutover was staged is not established.

architecture.style: Modular monolith with explicit control-plane / execution-plane separation
key_patterns: Control plane (mutable config) separated from execution plane (immutable sent evidence)
Execution runs freeze channel bindings, template versions, approval state and audience metadata
Per-recipient records store rendered subject/body and variable values at send time
Queue handoff via Azure Service Bus; no send occurs in a request lifecycle
Provider adapters behind a common interface
Idempotency enforced by composite database unique constraints
Provider webhook reconciliation kept deliberately distinct from internal execution state
architecture.auth: Invite-only Google Identity Services / OIDC, server-side token verification, Workspace-domain enforced, SessionAuthGuard + RolesGuard, roles StandardUser/Manager/Admin, no local passwords

integrations.name: External Service Comms API
integrations.purpose: Inbound API for other internal systems (/mail, /sms, /whatsapp)

integrations.name: UCP Monitor API
integrations.purpose: ucp-execution-summary endpoint for an external dashboard, bounded to 3 calendar days

workflows: Campaign lifecycle: Draft -> submit for review (named Admin reviewer) -> approve/reject/withdraw -> live
Template versioning with independent per-version approval
Audience sourcing via CSV upload or polled preset SQL flow with per-day dedupe
Execution: freeze approved state into a run -> create durable per-recipient records -> enqueue -> processor invokes provider adapter
Delivery reconciliation from provider webhooks into execution events
Channel-aware suppression and eligibility evaluated before send
Scheduled dispatch with unique (schedule, slot) guarantee
External Service Comms: API-key authenticated transactional sending with threading and per-client rate limits
Daily, operational and weekly audit/notification reporting

business_impact.why_quantified_before_after_is_impossibl: The legacy estate recorded no send-level outcome data: Apps Scripts logged failures only to console via an unimplemented notifier and persisted only per-process 'row picked up' markers. There is no artefact from which legacy volume, failure rate, or missed-customer counts could be reconstructed. The qualitative, code-corroborated before/after is the ceiling of what is claimable.

engineering_challenges.name: Snapshot reproducibility under mutable configuration
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Campaigns and templates stay editable, but a message sent last month must remain reproducible exactly as rendered; every downstream view must read the snapshot rather than the live entity.

engineering_challenges.name: Idempotency across four independent trigger paths
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Continuous polling, at-least-once queue delivery, overlapping schedules and retries make duplicate sends the default failure mode; solved structurally with composite unique constraints rather than application checks.

engineering_challenges.name: Distributed state across systems that disagree
engineering_challenges.why_hard: 212,492 provider webhook events arrive out of order against 85,482 sends; the design deliberately preserves the distinction between internal execution state and external provider evidence rather than collapsing them.

engineering_challenges.name: Unreliable external dependencies
engineering_challenges.why_hard: An external source database is polled ~149k times with stale-lock recovery for crashed pollers; provider failures captured with dedicated error context.

engineering_challenges.name: Provider abstraction proven in production
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Five adapters run concurrently with per-sender and per-campaign routing, not a single-vendor wrapper.

engineering_challenges.name: Domain complexity
engineering_challenges.why_hard: 34 models, 66 migrations, 155 routes, channel-aware suppression, throttle windows, blackout periods, template variable validation, per-client rate limits.

decisions.problem: Mutable campaign config versus immutable sent-message evidence
decisions.decision: Separate control plane from execution plane; freeze runs from approved state
decisions.tradeoffs: Significant data duplication and more complex queries
decisions.result: Every send reproducible; full audit chain in production

decisions.problem: HTTP request lifecycle cannot own delivery of thousands of messages
decisions.decision: Queue-backed execution via Azure Service Bus
decisions.reasoning: Stated non-negotiable boundary in project guidance
decisions.tradeoffs: At-least-once semantics force idempotency work; larger operational surface
decisions.result: 1,598-message peak day handled; 4 cancellations across 5,261 runs

decisions.problem: Service decomposition for a solo-maintained system
decisions.reasoning: Deployable and operable by one engineer while preserving boundaries
decisions.tradeoffs: One service reached 10,463 lines — real maintainability cost
decisions.result: Boundaries exist for later extraction; the large file is known debt

decisions.decision: Enforce invariants in the database, not the application
decisions.reasoning: Structural guarantee survives new code paths
decisions.tradeoffs: A batch containing internal duplicates aborted whole syncs until handled
decisions.result: Zero duplicate dispatches across 1,146 schedule slots

decisions.problem: Speed of UI delivery without ceding ownership of business logic
decisions.decision: Use Lovable for UI scaffolding only, governed by AGENTS.md
decisions.reasoning: Explicit rule that AI never owns business logic or auth
decisions.tradeoffs: Generated code required substantial subsequent rework (-10,248 lines)
decisions.result: Bot activity ceased after one week; all later work hand-directed

decisions.problem: The strategic goal - every company communication through one platform - fails if each calling system must be rewritten to adopt it. Adoption friction, not capability, was the binding constraint.
decisions.decision: Reimplement the legacy iros-mail HTTP contract verbatim inside UCP (POST /api/mail, bearer-key auth, identical field names) while discarding its EJS/local-microservice internals; extend the pattern to /api/sms and /api/whatsapp.
decisions.reasoning: Callers repoint a base URL instead of rewriting an integration, so consolidation proceeds incrementally rather than as a coordinated cutover.
decisions.tradeoffs: Legacy field shapes (mjml, processAt, attachment) are carried into a new system's public contract and constrain it for as long as those clients exist - long-term design debt accepted for migration velocity.
decisions.result: 22 registered clients, 18,113 emails, monthly volume 47 -> 7,075 in four months. The decision that converted a stated strategic goal into measured adoption.

problems_solved.title: UK date format silently flipping in customer communications
problems_solved.situation: Legacy preset flows map source dates into customer-facing insurance emails
problems_solved.problem: new Date() applied US MM/dd to dd/MM/yyyy strings, so 5 August became 8 May; wrong only for day values <= 12, invisible most of the month
problems_solved.investigation: Traced to a private toLegacyDateString helper duplicated in the variable mapper
problems_solved.solution: Explicit Luxon parsing in a shared legacy-flow.helpers.ts plus a regression test named for the failure mode
problems_solved.result: Commit 22d52e0, 2026-08-18: 146 insertions, 30 deletions, 3 files, 98 lines of test

problems_solved.title: Duplicate source keys crashing the sync
problems_solved.situation: Preset SQL flows pull batches from an external source database
problems_solved.problem: A batch containing two rows with the same dedupe key aborted the entire sync via the unique constraint
problems_solved.investigation: Reproduced with a duplicate outstanding-payment batch
problems_solved.solution: Duplicate-tolerant handling in syncSourceItems with a regression test
problems_solved.result: Commit 2026-06-14; production now 149,065 successes against 256 failures

problems_solved.title: Circular foreign keys blocking database restore
problems_solved.problem: Template.currentVersionId, User.departmentId and two Department self-references form cycles defeating ordered restore
problems_solved.solution: Sync script drops those four constraints before restore and restores them after

problems_solved.title: Permission model corrected: withdraw-review
problems_solved.problem: canWithdrawCampaignReview granted the action to any Admin, so the assigned reviewer could retract the submitter's own review request
problems_solved.solution: Narrowed to draft owner plus collaborators; reviewers approve or reject instead
problems_solved.result: Permission check and error message corrected

lessons: Pushing invariants into database constraints produced a silently correct result 1,146 times
Freezing execution state early made reconciliation and audit straightforward rather than archaeological
Writing an agent-instruction file before heavy AI tooling use kept generated code inside intended boundaries
Treating documentation as a same-task deliverable kept it current
A 10,463-line service should have been split earlier along its four real responsibilities
Test coverage should grow with the domain rather than clustering only around known-subtle areas
Ban new Date(string) on business input by lint rule, not by convention
Two logging paths recording the same event at different granularities will eventually be read as contradicting each other; metric definitions need the same care as schema

The highest-leverage decision was not a feature: preserving the legacy HTTP contract verbatim meant other teams could adopt by changing a URL. Consolidation goals fail on adoption friction long before they fail on capability.

The legacy estate could not be measured because it never recorded outcomes - which makes its own replacement impossible to quantify. Systems should record what they did from day one; the absence is only discovered when it is too late to backfill.

problem_statement: Communications scattered across systems with no central visibility
No way to see which customers had been contacted or whether messages arrived
Processes broke; messages silently lost; staff re-triggered emails manually
No reporting or communication statistics for executives
C-level (CEO/CTO) demand for consolidation into one monitored place

corroborated_in_code.evidence: notifyExecutionFailed in old-google-scripts/iros-process-one/functions.gs is an unimplemented stub containing '//todo send email' and a console.error; runAll catches per-function errors and continues

corroborated_in_code.claim: No send-level record of what went to whom
corroborated_in_code.evidence: Zero occurrences of SpreadsheetApp/appendRow/getRange/setValue across the Apps Script estate; only ten per-process wp_* marker tables storing created/ref/polno/reason/raw-row-JSON
iros-mail exposes API-key HTTP endpoints only; Apps Scripts have no UI surface

origin_and_stakeholder_context.important_nuance: It is NOT true that the legacy estate stored nothing - per-process markers existed and iros-mail kept its own EmailRecord store in MongoDB. The accurate, narrower claim is that there was no unified, queryable, cross-channel record of what was sent to a given customer, and no interface to ask the question.

requirements_to_capability.requirement: All company communications in one place
requirements_to_capability.capability: 5 provider adapters, 3 channels behind one approval/suppression model; 22 external clients routed through the platform API

requirements_to_capability.requirement: Visibility and monitoring of what is going out
requirements_to_capability.capability: Dashboard overview, campaign message search/export, 364,430-event audit log, ucp-execution-summary monitor API

requirements_to_capability.requirement: Look up a customer and see every communication sent to them
requirements_to_capability.capability: GET /customer-communications - UNION ALL across CampaignExecutionRecipient and TransactionalEmail, with dedicated UI page

requirements_to_capability.requirement: Reporting and communication statistics for executives
requirements_to_capability.capability: Daily summary, operational report (HTML + export), weekly audit report services

requirements_to_capability.requirement: Other internal systems must send through this service
requirements_to_capability.capability: POST /api/mail preserves the legacy iros-mail contract verbatim

stakeholder_recognition.claim: Commended on this project by the CEO and CTO on several occasions
stakeholder_recognition.qualification: Uncorroborated. Usable in interview as 'I'm told...'; do not put in writing as fact until a dated written source exists.

legacy_systems_replaced.name: Google Apps Script estate (iros-process-one, iros-process-two)
legacy_systems_replaced.technology: Google Apps Script, time-driven triggers (runEveryMinute/Hour/Day), JDBC to MySQL
legacy_systems_replaced.replacement_status: 11 flows reimplemented as UCP preset-flow adapters: dreq_inception, dreq, canc_acknow, canc_chase, os_payments_new, renew_acknowledge, renew_nocontact, ad_hoc_docs, rta7_emails, rta7_rmail, renew_invite
legacy_systems_replaced.open_items: 8 functions referenced by legacy code.gs have no implementation in checked-in source (createStatusReport, createIrevStatusReport, createPremierStatusReport, sendErrorsEmail, sendCancErrorsEmail, processUkisMid, updateErrorsData, updateCancErrorsData) and are tracked as a separate discovery track

legacy_systems_replaced.name: iros-mail
legacy_systems_replaced.technology: .NET 8 isolated Azure Functions, EJS + MJML rendering, MongoDB email records, Azure Blob template/image storage, SMTP via MailKit, scheduled-send and failed-email-reschedule workers
legacy_systems_replaced.replacement_status: HTTP contract absorbed into UCP as POST /api/mail with identical bearer-key auth and field names, while discarding the EJS/local-microservice architecture
